name: The Symphony Macro-System
tagline: A historical rhyme on the mini-system fad of the 80s and 90s. Tall (150cm), under 20cm deep, 36cm wide. True full-range high-efficiency. Three application variants: In-Room, On-Wall (sconce-inspired), In-Wall (pre-primed paper).
description: Sub-bass that dedicated premium subwoofers can't reach, at low volume. The first product where the No-Nails engineering process is fully visible: a single 8" woofer transmission-line tuned to reach below 30Hz, beryllium-alloy HF mounted in dustcap position, every domain contributing modestly.

variants.name: In-Wall
variants.differentiator: Pre-primed paper surface, ready for the enviro-design team's finish coat

roadmap_notes: CoGS ~$200 at low-1000s; refactors to <$100. **PR stunt: Symphony submitted for review at $29,990 first, corrected post-submission to $2,990 retail** — anchor the price ceiling, then drop the ladder. NAD 3020 anchor: $89 in 1978 ≈ $432 in 2026 — the bargain that minted a global brand. Certifications budgeted at **~$30K combined (ETL/FCC/CE)** per SKU.

key_differentiators: Transmission-line single-woofer down to <30Hz at low SPL
No-Nails engineering process — every discipline contributes modestly
Three variants (In-Room, On-Wall sconce, In-Wall paper) on shared platform
PR stunt: $29,990 review tier, corrected to $2,990 retail
